lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit for my son, Alex. He's my only child, so just the one.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex! I have a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, his eligibility depends on his current situation.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or on an approved training course? Or has he left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He actually left school recently, but he's just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Just to clarify a couple of things:

1. When did Alex turn 17 (or when will he turn 18)?
2. How long ago did Alex leave school?
3. When you say he's "signed up with the local careers service," is this a government-approved training scheme or careers advice programme, or is it more informal career guidance/counselling?

I ask because there are specific rules about what qualifies as an "approved training course" for Child Benefit purposes.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
He turned 17 back in March. He left school at the end of the summer term, so that was a few months ago now. 

As for the careers service, he registered with them shortly after leaving school - it's the official careers service run by the local authority. They're helping him work out his options and next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for those details.

One more important question: Has Alex registered with the local authority careers service (or a similar qualifying body) as someone who is **not in education, employment, or training** – and is he available for education, training, or work? 

I ask because in the UK, Child Benefit can continue for a young person aged 16 or 17 who has left education or training, provided they register with an approved careers service or similar body and are not in full-time paid work (24 hours or more per week). This is sometimes referred to as the "child benefit extension period."

Also, is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, that's exactly it - he registered with the careers service after leaving school because he's not in education or work right now. He's available and looking at his options for what to do next.

And no, he's not working at all at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming all of that. That's very helpful.

Just one final question: Are you currently living in the UK, and is Alex living with you (or are you contributing to the cost of looking after him if he lives elsewhere)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**Alex qualifies under the Child Benefit extension period** because:
- He is 17 years old (between 16 and 18)
- Although he has left school, he has registered with the local authority careers service
- He is not currently in education, employment, or training, and is available for education, training, or work
- He is not working 24 hours or more per week

**You meet the other requirements** because:
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you, so you are responsible for him

**Important things to note:**
- This eligibility will continue until Alex turns 18, or until he starts full-time paid work (24 hours or more per week), or starts full-time education or training – whichever happens first
- If Alex's circumstances change (e.g., he starts working, goes to college, or leaves the careers service), you'll need to report this as it may affect your entitlement

If you're not already claiming Child Benefit, you can apply through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?

Additionally, the claimant lives in the UK (Manchester) and Alex lives at home with them, satisfying the residency and responsibility requirements. Child Benefit can continue under these circumstances until Alex turns 18 or starts full-time work/education/training, whichever comes first.
